observed_facts: 2026-10-20, 21 and 22 whole-calendar-day returned PNG counts are 1221, 922 and 401; 2026-10-23 through 23:36 local has 373. These include pauses and art corrections and are not qualified-source counts.
Today 12-16 and 16-20 local returned 95 and 93 PNGs, or 23.75 and 23.25 per hour; 20-23:36 returned 59, approximately 16.4 per hour, about 30 percent lower than 16-20.
Successful dispatch-to-recorded-return median was 32.00 seconds on Oct22 and 43.08 seconds on Oct23, but Oct20/21 were 45.38/44.13 seconds. This is not a monotonic multi-day service slowdown.
Today has 435 actual dispatches, 373 PNG returns and 62 tool errors. All 435 records had a durable final result at the observation cutoff.

Approximately 13.7 hours of between-batch no-dispatch intervals remain after the 03:14 local restart. That interval class includes input preparation, review, orchestration and other work; timestamps alone cannot allocate it precisely to each activity.
Today has a recorded successful dispatch-to-return outlier of 1802.5 seconds at 23:01 local. The interval includes transport and client receipt persistence; no server-side timing is available.

Qualified-source snapshots grew from 3838 at 09:50 to 3941 at 21:00, an increase of 103 over about 11.17 hours. This is net registered art qualification, distinct from PNG output, with pending reviews and repairs still outstanding.
causal_assessment: The dominant observed wall-time loss is between batches. Source verification, fine-detail review, preparing small batches and client orchestration are work categories actually performed, but their individual durations were not instrumented, so no exact per-category attribution is claimed.
Longer typical successful recorded intervals and occasional long waits also reduce throughput; this establishes client-observed waiting, not the server-side cause.
Tool errors reduce returned PNGs per dispatch; cooled retries retain the original payload and consume lifetime quota, and cannot be replaced by altered requests to speed up output.

Fine art repairs can return another PNG without increasing qualified-source progress. This phase includes repeated collar, mouth, background opacity, note and outfit corrections; difficult or ambiguous results remain rejected or pending.
Existing checkpoint push/readback network recoveries are documented separately. No measured allocation proves that they account for all between-batch gaps.
execution_change: Prepare and actually review the next allowed HIGH input set while the current single builtin lane is running; apply decisions only at the sole importer's safe boundary, then dispatch the next batch promptly. No extra image lanes, altered refusals, reduced quality gate or completed-source inflation.
limits: Unknown historical interrupted calls are excluded from measured occupied duration; they are not treated as continuously running until now. The report is a time-bounded local ledger observation, not live game acceptance, overall completion or a claim of server throttling.
